anomalies.observed: U4 pin 4 (GND1) and pin 5 (GND2) are both connected to net GND; U24 pin 4 (GND1) and pin 5 (GND2) are both connected to net GND.
anomalies.expected: GND1 and GND2 should be on separate isolated ground nets to maintain galvanic isolation between the logic side and the CAN bus side.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation of the CAN transceivers is defeated, allowing ground loops and common-mode voltages to pass between the logic and bus sides, which can damage components and corrupt communication.

anomalies.observed: R28 connects U24 CANL (/NET0075) to SW5 pin 1, which connects to SW5 pin 3 (U4 CANH /NET0209). R83 connects U4 CANL (/NET0078) to SW5 pin 2, which connects to SW5 pin 4 (U24 CANH /NET0022).
anomalies.expected: R28 should connect U24 CANH to U24 CANL, and R83 should connect U4 CANH to U4 CANL, so that each 120R termination resistor is across its own CAN bus.
anomalies.impact: When termination is enabled via SW5, the two isolated CAN buses are connected through 120R resistors, bridging them and preventing proper termination of either bus, leading to communication errors.

anomalies.observed: D45 pin 4 (A2) is on NET0102; D45 pin 2 (K2) is on Net-(D45-K2); R34 is connected between Net-(D45-K2) and NET0102.
anomalies.expected: R34 should connect Net-(D45-K2) to GND, so that the LED is in series with the current-limiting resistor to ground.
anomalies.impact: The second LED in D45 will never illuminate because there is no path to ground; R34 is in parallel with the LED instead of in series, so the LED is effectively shorted and the resistor only loads the NET0102 signal.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple anomalies: the isolated CAN transceivers have their isolated grounds tied together, the CAN termination resistors are cross-connected between the two buses, and a dual LED has its current-limiting resistor wired to the wrong net, preventing it from lighting.
